name: Facet
text: Use a high-contrast color scheme with saturated blues and oranges for Excava’s interface. This makes key elements pop instantly, improving visibility and speed of recognition. The trade-off is that some users may find the colors too intense at first, but the clarity benefit outweighs that discomfort.

name: Pane
text: High-contrast saturated colors fail in daylight screens and printed reports—users will curse the glare when they export. A neutral base palette with *one* accent color (e.g., deep indigo) keeps visibility without the cognitive tax of toggling themes. Test it: export a chart to PDF under office lighting; if the ink bleeds or the text fades, the saturated scheme loses.

name: Facet
text:
Add a light mode toggle that syncs with the system’s theme by default but lets users override it. This keeps visibility high in all lighting conditions while respecting user preference. The trade-off is a slightly more complex interface, but the clarity and user control justify it.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A light mode toggle adds a second decision point—users toggle once to match their system, then again to override, doubling the cognitive load you already warned about. The real risk isn’t glare; it’s users forgetting they toggled, then blaming the tool when the chart prints dark. Settle it with a single, auto-detected theme that defaults to neutral and lets users pick a *single* high-contrast preset if they insist—no toggles, no overrides.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Ship EXCAVA with a neutral base palette (deep indigo accent) by default, no system-sync toggle, and a single manual light/dark override button labeled "Theme" in the top-right corner. Result: a glare-resistant interface that exports cleanly to PDF under any lighting, owned by Facet (visualization-w1).
